processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Parent solution-treatment step (proc_st-1050c-2h) preceding the 490°C aging of the 0.59% Si sample.
Age hardening at 490°C for 63 h used to compare κ-carbide size/number density between 0.59% and 1.56% Si steels.

structures.overall_structure: Dark austenite matrix with relatively sparse nanoscale κ-carbide precipitates arranged in patchy clusters (dark-field TEM)

phases_present.morphology: nanosized bright precipitates, sparse and patchy clusters

precipitates.distribution: homogeneous coherent precipitation in austenite; in this 0.59% Si sample the precipitates are sparse and patchy, appearing smaller/fewer than in the 1.56% Si steel

interfaces.phase_evolution: κ-carbide precipitation during aging; homogeneous coherent precipitation of nanosized κ-carbide in the austenite matrix
interfaces.interface_notes: κ-carbide has cube-on-cube orientation relationship with austenite: ⟨100⟩κ // ⟨100⟩γ and {001}κ // {001}γ.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: aged 63 h at 490°C; 10 nm scale bar; selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern inset
characterization_methods.purpose: compare κ-carbide precipitate size and number density between 0.59% and 1.56% Si steels
characterization_methods.key_findings: 0.59% Si steel shows relatively sparse, patchy nanoscale κ-carbide precipitates; precipitate size and number density appear smaller/fewer than in the 1.56% Si steel

unmapped_findings: Alloy-level porosity note (Fig. 15, b0079): the 0.59% Si low-P steel had a total inclusion density similar to the 1.07% and 1.56% Si steels (62–78 inclusions/mm²), but its porosity (micro-defects) was more than twice that of the 1.07% Si steel and almost double that of the 1.56% Si steel; this higher porosity was proposed as the reason for the 0.59% Si steel's lower aged dynamic fracture toughness. This is a casting/material-level observation, not specific to the 490°C/63 h aging.
